purpose: Crofelemer is used to relieve non-infectious diarrhea in adults with HIV/AIDS who are taking antiretroviral medications. It helps reduce the number of loose or watery stools you have each day. It is not meant to treat diarrhea caused by an infection.
how_it_works: Your intestines normally move water and salts in and out of your gut lining through tiny channels. When these channels are overactive, too much water rushes into your intestines, causing watery diarrhea. Crofelemer works by blocking two of these channels, which slows down the flow of water into the gut and helps make your stools more normal and solid. It works right in the gut and is not absorbed much into your bloodstream.
common_side_effects: Most people tolerate this medication well. The most common side effects include upper respiratory infections like a cold, cough, flatulence (gas), bronchitis, and stomach pain. Some people may also notice nausea or urinary tract infections.
warnings: Tell your doctor if your diarrhea might be caused by an infection, because this medicine will not help with infectious diarrhea and could delay proper treatment. Let your doctor know about all other medications you take and if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, since safety in these situations is not fully established. This medication is not approved for use in children.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is one 125 mg delayed-release tablet taken by mouth twice a day, morning and evening. You can take it with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush or chew it. Take it regularly every day for the best results.
